requirement: Lithium batteries shipped by air or sea must pass UN 38.3 testing (8 tests: altitude simulation, thermal test, vibration, shock, external short circuit, impact/crush, overcharge, forced discharge) before international transport. A UN 38.3 test summary report must accompany each shipment.
requirement_summary: Lithium batteries must pass all 8 UN 38.3 tests (altitude, thermal, vibration, shock, short circuit, impact, overcharge, forced discharge) for international transport

regulation_source.section: ST/SG/AC.10/11/Rev.7 - Tests and Criteria Part III

evidence_required.description: UN 38.3 test report covering all 8 tests (T.1-T.8) with pass results
UN 38.3 Test Summary Report (required since July 2023 for all lithium battery shipments)

remediation: 1. Submit lithium battery to UN 38.3 accredited testing lab for all 8 tests. 2. Obtain UN 38.3 Test Summary Report. 3. Ensure MSDS and transport classification documents are prepared. 4. Declare as Class 9 dangerous goods with proper lithium battery transport labels.

requirement: Lithium batteries shipped by air must have State of Charge (SoC) not exceeding 30% of rated capacity. Each package must bear the lithium battery handling label (as per IATA PI 966/967) and be declared as Class 9 dangerous goods. Effective 2026, this requirement is strictly enforced for all international air freight.
requirement_summary: Air-shipped lithium batteries must have SoC ≤30% and bear proper Class 9 dangerous goods labels per IATA PI 966/967

regulation_source.section: PI 966 / PI 967 - Air Transport SoC Limit

evidence_required.description: Battery SoC verification document showing charge level ≤30% before air shipment
MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheet) for lithium battery
Transport classification report declaring Class 9 dangerous goods

remediation: 1. Discharge battery to ≤30% SoC before air shipment. 2. Prepare MSDS and transport classification report. 3. Apply lithium battery handling label per IATA requirements. 4. Declare as Class 9 dangerous goods on air waybill. 5. Use UN-approved packaging.
